cues.text: Your app emits events.
The rest of your stack expects webhooks.
Which means retries. Signing. Health checks. Every time.
So teams build it: a Redis queue, retry crons, signing code, dashboards, alerts.
And events still quietly get lost.
With Sparrow, it's just Postgres.
Sparrow: webhook delivery you run yourself.
Let's follow one event, order.created,
cues.say: Let's follow one event, order dot created,

cues.text: from push, to delivered.
Step one: your service pushes the event.
One POST. Sparrow stores it and answers right away.
Push it again with the same idempotency key?
You get the original back. No duplicate.
Step two: fan-out.
Sparrow finds every subscription that matches:
the event name, the consumer, even labels like env=prod,
cues.say: the event name, the consumer, even labels like env equals prod,

cues.text: and queues one delivery for each. Right in Postgres.
Step three: build the request.
The standard envelope, or your own shape with a Go template.
Headers too, even an API token, encrypted at rest.
Any method: POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
So one event can call almost any HTTP API.
And every request is signed: HMAC or Ed25519.
cues.say: And every request is signed: H-MAC, or E-D twenty-five-five-nineteen.

cues.text: Recipes are exactly that, pre-packaged.
PagerDuty, Twilio, SendGrid, ClickHouse and more, one YAML file each.
One command applies one: sparrow use pagerduty.
cues.say: One command applies one. Sparrow, use PagerDuty.

cues.text: Step four: send, and read the answer.
Every failure lands in one of ten categories.
Server errors and timeouts? Worth another try.
DNS, TLS, or a 4xx? Retrying won't help,
cues.say: DNS, TLS, or a four-hundred error? Retrying won't help,

cues.text: so Sparrow stops.
Step five: back off.
By default, three retries: one minute, two, then four.
Doubling every time.
And a 429, slow down?
cues.say: And a four twenty-nine, slow down?

cues.text: Sparrow waits out Retry-After, without spending an attempt.
Meanwhile, every webhook carries a health state.
Healthy, above ninety percent success.
Degraded, between eighty and ninety.
Five failures in a row? Unhealthy.
And every change can email your on-call.
Nothing is a mystery.
Every attempt is recorded: status, timing, error category.
When the partner is back, retry it by ID.
And you don't have to dig through logs.
A dashboard ships inside the same binary: webhooks, events, deliveries, health.
Plus a consumer portal, so your customers manage their own webhooks.
And OpenTelemetry traces every event, end to end.
So what does it need to run?
Just PostgreSQL. The queue lives there too. No Redis, no broker.
And it's MIT licensed: free to run, fork and ship. No per-message pricing.
How does that stack up?
Svix and Convoy add Redis. Hookdeck's core is SaaS.
Sparrow is fully MIT, with dual signing, recipes, a portal and self-monitoring.
So, where did order.created end up?
cues.say: So, where did order dot created end up?

cues.text: Exactly where you sent it.
Push once. Sparrow does the rest.
One Go binary. One Postgres.
